findings.draft_text: 最终文件/ID与从头确定性执行一致
findings.evidence: fixture_compile.rs creates fresh run_id/release_id UUIDs and started_at; reports include run/ release IDs and timestamps. DATA_CONTRACTS says production IDs are generated and persisted, and fixture entity IDs are fixed.
findings.clarification: Compare frozen normative output files and stable fixture/knowledge IDs; preserve the same persisted Run/Release identity during recovery. New independent baseline runs may have distinct Run/Release/attempt IDs and audit times, which must be fully retained and checked for ownership rather than normalized away without a declared rule. Also freeze the finite graph and specify changed-dependent units vs unaffected reusable units.

findings.topic: Budget levels and attempt settlement identity
findings.draft_text: 坏单元耗尽预算后可定位，不阻断独立单元
findings.evidence: FR-36 isolates bad work, while FR-38 requires stopping new requests at shared budget cap. Same response body bytes can belong to two different paid attempts.
findings.clarification: Define WorkUnit retry allocation and shared Run/global commitment budget separately. An exhausted unit may not block independent units while shared budget remains; shared budget exhaustion must prevent every new request. Settlement idempotency is bound to persisted Run/WorkUnit/request-attempt identity, not response content SHA alone; two distinct attempts returning identical bytes must both be accounted for.

findings.topic: Initial managed baseline and finite operation scope
findings.evidence: FR-34 applies default read-only to an existing Vault without an old release baseline; D09 permits only new test roots before manual protection. Publishing needs a trusted previous baseline.
findings.clarification: Retain read-only behavior for existing or unknown Vaults with no baseline. State how the brand-new owned test collection creates its first baseline or explicitly imports a verified ordinary fixture release, with exact content/owner/source binding. Freeze a finite managed-file inventory, dependency set, and supported add/edit/move/delete/rollback cases; unfamiliar files and operations remain outside management.
